title: Next.js Static Export, App Router & Build-Time Data Architecture
description: Understand how generateStaticParams, Server Components, and static export constraints work together on edge CDNs.
author: Qodlume Editorial

questions.prompt: When Next.js is configured with `output: 'export'`, how are dynamic route segments like `app/quiz/[date]/page.tsx` resolved?

options.text: They are rendered on-demand by a Node.js server whenever a browser requests an unknown date.
generateStaticParams() executes at build time to pre-render HTML and RSC payloads for each returned parameter set.
Dynamic routes are forbidden when output: 'export' is enabled.
The browser directly reads the server filesystem using fs.readFileSync at runtime.

questions.explanation: With static export (`output: 'export'`), Next.js runs `generateStaticParams()` during `next build` and emits static HTML/payload files for every returned route parameter.

questions.prompt: Why must privileged secrets (such as database passwords or GitHub Personal Access Tokens) NEVER be placed in `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` environment variables?

options.text: Next.js refuses to compile if any NEXT_PUBLIC_ variable exceeds 32 characters.
NEXT_PUBLIC_* values are inlined directly into the client-side JavaScript bundle sent to every visitor's browser.
NEXT_PUBLIC_* variables are only readable inside middleware.
They are automatically uploaded to public npm registries.

questions.explanation: During compilation, Next.js replaces references to `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_*` with literal strings in the client bundle, making them visible to anyone inspecting browser network traffic or sources.
